final_answer: mRNA vaccines work by delivering a piece of genetic material called messenger RNA (mRNA) into the body. This mRNA contains instructions for cells to produce a harmless piece of the virus's spike protein. Once the mRNA enters the cells, it is used to create the spike protein, which is then displayed on the cell surface. The immune system recognizes this protein as foreign and mounts an immune response, producing antibodies and memory cells. This prepares the body to fight off future infections by the actual virus.
